defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: src/scene.py:37 important - remove(new_m) runs before searching, so new_m is dropped when old_m is missing and ValueError is raised
src/scene.py:37 important - remove(new_m) at current recursion level strips top-level new_m when old_m is nested
src/scene.py:37 important - list.remove only removes first occurrence, leaving duplicates of new_m
tests/test_scene.py:30 nit - no test for replace(obj, obj); remove drops the object and the search then raises a misleading ValueError
votes.evidence_quote: With the current code, line 37's `remove` drops the object, then the search fails to find `old_m` (it was just removed), raising the misleading `ValueError("Could not find")`.
votes.justification: The review's nit names the self-replace case and gives the right cause: the dedup `remove` at line 37 drops the object before the search, so the search fails and raises ValueError. It labels this a nit about missing test coverage, but the behaviour, cause and location all match the known defect.
